purpose: Determine whether an official ECB quantitative internal-consistency materiality rule can be applied to Romanian quarterly financial accounts for the narrow aggregate reference-mode acceptability test, independently of the residual magnitudes already observed.

official_evidence.document: Euro area quarterly financial accounts 2013 quality report
exact_semantics: Horizontal consistency is equality between assets summed over relevant sectors and liabilities summed over relevant sectors.
Discrepancies of less than EUR 10 million are considered acceptable in the national data.

official_evidence.document: Euro area and national quarterly financial accounts – Quality report 2024
exact_semantics: Internal consistency concerns accounting identities and hierarchical relationships between aggregates and components.
Horizontal consistency is equality between the sum of financial assets and the sum of liabilities for each financial instrument.
The national financial accounts datasets transmitted to the ECB are internally consistent except for minor issues.
Internal discrepancies and unexplained negative stocks of more than EUR 10 million were observed in a few countries and were generally corrected in later transmissions.
The ECB runs quality checks on all quarterly financial accounts received from EU Member States.
official_evidence.role: Current continuity and direct EU/Romania scope.

scientific_boundary.interpretation: The ECB materiality rule may govern whether the disseminated aggregate series is acceptable as an observed behaviour-over-time reference mode. It does not make the public data an exact accounting spine.
